title: Iter-3 price injection diverges from companion-event design; comments stale
description: Iter-3 wires Order.price in dataLayer.ts:209-216 by shifting orderIdStr right 64 bits ('price is the upper 64 bits' per the inline comment). But marketStats.ts:53-54 still reads 'For bids, the order_id decode is tautologically correct against test fixtures but wrong against real chain order_ids. Prefer injected price.' implying the injected price comes from a companion OrderInfo/OrderPlaced event — and types.ts:72 doubles down ('Injected from companion OrderInfo/OrderPlaced event. Preferred over order_id decode.'). In reality the injection is just another order_id decode using the same input as decodeBidPrice/decodeAskPrice; the data layer never joins against event payloads. So three formulae now claim to decode 'price from order_id': dataLayer's `BigInt(id) >> 64n`, marketStats.decodeAskPrice's `(id & (ASK_BIT_OFFSET-1n)) / PRICE_BIT_OFFSET`, and marketStats.decodeBidPrice's `U64_MAX - id / PRICE_BIT_OFFSET`. Either (a) all three are equivalent on chain inputs and two are dead, or (b) they disagree and the test suite cannot tell because it never feeds a real chain order_id through both paths.
impact: Reader cannot determine the canonical decoding rule from the source. The 'CR-2 fix' comment in dataLayer.ts:208 promises the injected path replaces the fixture-shaped decode, but the documentation in marketStats.ts and types.ts both promise the injection comes from event data — neither matches what was implemented. A future maintainer fixing the bid encoding (the original CR-2 bug) will read the comments, look for OrderInfo→Order plumbing, find none, and either rewrite the wrong layer or add a redundant join. The doc/code drift recreates the original confusion the iter-2 review surfaced.
recommendation: Either (1) align comments to reality: rewrite the marketStats.ts:53-54 and types.ts:72 doc-comments to say 'Injected by the data layer from order_id high 64 bits'; delete the marketStats.decodeBidPrice and decodeAskPrice fallbacks since the injected price is now always populated when orders come from the chain; or (2) actually do the OrderInfo→Order join the docs describe (cross-reference Order.order_id with OrderInfo.order_id captured by buildQueryEventsFn) and remove the bit-shift. Option (1) is the smaller change; option (2) is what the comments currently promise.

title: main.tsx still mutates deps after construction; module-level cachedPackageId persists
description: Iter-2 R2-001 (high) flagged that main.tsx builds AppDeps then mutates `deps.loadManifest` to wrap a module-level `let cachedPackageId` so fetchPoolStats can later read it. Iter-3 left this entirely unchanged. The wiring still depends on the runtime invariant 'loadManifest must resolve before any fetchPoolStats call'; nothing in the type system encodes that. fetchPoolStats called first silently fetches against packageId='' (suix_queryEvents will reject the empty package or return no events), and the App will render 'no fills' rather than an error.
impact: Same as iter-2: the dependency-injection contract is violated by a side-effect through a closed-over module-level mutable. With iter-3's price-injection now landing inside the fetchPoolStats call path, any future ordering bug becomes harder to detect because both the manifest load AND the price decoding now silently degrade together. Reassigning a property on the deps the App will receive is a React-foreign idiom and a documented antipattern in DI systems where deps are a read-only contract.
recommendation: Construct the deps as a single object whose closures share a memoized manifest promise: `const manifestPromise = (async () => parseManifest(await (await fetch(MANIFEST_URL)).json(), MANIFEST_URL))(); const deps: AppDeps = { loadManifest: () => manifestPromise, fetchPoolStats: async (d) => fetchSinglePoolStats(RPC_URL, (await manifestPromise).deepbookPackageId, d, Date.now()) };`. No mutation, no module-level let, the dependency is a cached promise. Same fix as iter-2 R2-001.

title: resolvePoolInnerFields still conflates four shape variants with implicit fallbacks
description: Iter-2 R2-004 (medium) flagged that resolvePoolInnerFields returns four structurally different sub-shapes under one signature and that one branch (`if 'book' in fields return fields`) is the production code-path branching on whether the response shape happens to match the T-014 unit-test fixture. Iter-3 did not touch this function; the four-way fallback ladder, the silent shape conflation, and the fixture-coupled production branch all persist verbatim. buildPoolInnerState still has to defensively `(field?.fields ?? field)` everywhere because the caller cannot tell which variant resolvePoolInnerFields returned.
impact: Same as iter-2: any future change to one of the four shapes silently switches branches. There is no logging to identify which path executed. Worst case, a real chain response that accidentally has a top-level `book` field (e.g. if a future Pool refactor inlines the Versioned) would skip the dynamic-field traversal and the code path would degrade silently. The fixture-aware branch makes this concrete.
recommendation: Same as iter-2 R2-004: split into two functions with crisp contracts — `resolvePoolInnerFromVersioned(rpcUrl, poolId): Promise<PoolInnerFields>` (production; throws if the Versioned/dynamic-field traversal does not yield a PoolInner) and `resolvePoolInnerFromDirect(obj): PoolInnerFields | null` (fixture/direct path). Have buildPoolInnerState branch explicitly. Or change the T-014 fixture to return the realistic Pool wrapper shape so the production code path has one variant.

title: App.tsx polling effect still duplicates initial-load pipeline; no cancel flag
description: Iter-2 R2-006 (medium) and R2-007 (medium) flagged that the initial-load effect (lines 41-87) and the polling effect (lines 91-125) duplicate ~30 lines of fetch+map+sentinel-card+poolErrors logic, and that the polling effect's `async` setInterval callback calls setState (line 121) after `await Promise.allSettled` without checking a `cancelled` flag (the cleanup only does clearInterval, not flag flip). Iter-3 did not touch App.tsx; both findings persist verbatim. The polling effect's stale-state-update hazard is one cleanup-callback line away.
impact: Same as iter-2: two effects re-implementing the same pipeline (maintenance hazard if sentinel-card shape or error-message extraction changes). Plus the polling setState fires after unmount in HMR or component-remount scenarios — React 19 warns rather than errors, but the bug is real (a stale interval tick from a previous mount can stomp on the new mount's state).
recommendation: Same as iter-2: extract `async function refreshAll(deps, pools): Promise<{ cards, poolErrors }>` and have both effects call it. Add a `let cancelled = false` to the polling effect, check it before setState in the async callback, and flip it in the cleanup callback. Or migrate polling to AbortController and pass signal through fetchPoolStats so in-flight RPC calls also abort.

title: dataLayer.ts still imports PoolCardData from a UI component file
description: Iter-2 R2-002 (medium) flagged that dataLayer.ts and main.tsx import PoolCardData from `components/PoolCard.js`, inverting the natural dependency direction (data layer depending on UI components). types.ts:14 still claims to be the home of `UI aggregate types (PoolCardData)` but PoolCardData is still declared in components/PoolCard.tsx:16-25. Iter-3 did not touch this; the half-applied single-source-of-truth fix from H-10 persists.
impact: Same as iter-2: structurally same shape as a circular dependency, broken only by file-load ordering accident. If anyone moves PoolCard or splits it into sub-components, the data layer breaks. The types.ts header comment is a documented lie until PoolCardData actually moves there.
recommendation: Same as iter-2 R2-002: move PoolCardData and SparklinePoint declarations to types.ts (which already documents itself as their home) and have PoolCard.tsx import them as `import type { PoolCardData, SparklinePoint } from '../types.js'`. Then dataLayer.ts imports PoolCardData from types.ts and the dependency direction matches the conceptual layering.

title: FillRecord/RawFillEvent twin types and no-op map survive iter-3
description: Iter-2 R2-003 (medium) flagged that FillRecord (fillAggregator.ts:9-14) and RawFillEvent (fillFetcher.ts:19-24) are structurally identical but declared in two modules, forcing the no-op map at dataLayer.ts:363-368. Iter-3 did not touch any of the three. The drift hazard remains: any new field added to one type but not the other is silently lost in the map. Documentation also still drifts — types.ts:14 mentions `RawFillEntry` (which exists in types.ts:94) but neither RawFillEvent nor FillRecord lives there.
impact: Same as iter-2: three places to update if a fifth field is ever needed. The map function is dead weight that would silently swallow any future field divergence.
recommendation: Same as iter-2 R2-003: move one canonical FillRecord (or RawFillEvent — pick one name) into types.ts. fillFetcher and fillAggregator both import it. Drop the no-op `.map(f => ({...}))` in dataLayer.ts:363-368 and pass rawFills directly to aggregateFills.

title: vite.config.ts manifest path still hard-coded to home-relative layout
description: Iter-2 R2-008 (low) flagged that the manifest disk path is hard-coded as `~/workspace/deepbook-sandbox/sandbox/deployments/localnet.json`, coupling the dev server to a specific workspace layout that the contract section 'Integration / sandbox contract' said should be configurable per-environment. Iter-3 did not touch vite.config.ts.
impact: Same as iter-2: friction for any developer whose checkout is not at exactly that path. Mitigated by the 404 response surfacing the expected path, so failure is debuggable.
recommendation: Same as iter-2 R2-008: read from an env var with the current default. `const MANIFEST_DISK_PATH = process.env.SANDBOX_MANIFEST_PATH ?? path.join(homedir(), 'workspace', 'deepbook-sandbox', 'sandbox', 'deployments', 'localnet.json');`. Document `SANDBOX_MANIFEST_PATH` in the README/runbook.

title: rpcId module-level mutable counter persists across iter-3
description: Iter-1 R2-010 (low) and iter-2 R2-009 (low) both flagged `let rpcId = 0;` at module scope. Iter-3 did not touch it. Inert today (JSON-RPC ids only need uniqueness within a connection), but global mutable state in a module that otherwise consciously injects state via args.
impact: Negligible at runtime. Slightly harder to reason about than necessary; would silently couple any future test that asserts on the id to test-execution order.
recommendation: Same as iter-2 R2-009: move into a closure created per `runDataLayer` invocation, or use `crypto.randomUUID()` / `Date.now()` for the id.

title: manifest.ts still re-exports types from types.ts; two canonical paths persist
description: Iter-2 R2-010 (low) flagged that manifest.ts re-exports PoolDescriptor and LoadedManifest from types.ts (line 22) while also importing them (line 23). Iter-3 did not touch it. App.tsx:14 and dataLayer.ts:19 still import these types from manifest.ts, perpetuating the dual canonical path.
impact: Same as iter-2: consolidator can no longer tell which file is canonical for these types just by reading imports. Doubles the surface area for type drift.
recommendation: Same as iter-2 R2-010: drop the re-export from manifest.ts, update App.tsx (line 14) and dataLayer.ts (line 19) to import directly from types.ts.
evidence:
export type { PoolDescriptor, LoadedManifest } from './types.js';
import type { LoadedManifest, PoolDescriptor } from './types.js';

title: fetchSinglePoolStats alias-as-fetchPoolStats still ships in iter-3
description: Iter-2 R2-011 (low) flagged the dual naming: `async function fetchPoolStats` (line 338) plus `export { fetchPoolStats as fetchSinglePoolStats };` (line 427). main.tsx imports it as fetchSinglePoolStats; runDataLayer (line 408) calls it as fetchPoolStats. Iter-3 did not pick a single name.
impact: Same as iter-2: reader friction for anyone tracing the function across module boundaries. Search-and-replace tooling will miss one of the two names.
recommendation: Same as iter-2 R2-011: pick one name. Drop the alias export.

title: Iter-3 price-decode try/catch swallows BigInt parse errors silently
description: The iter-3 patch wraps `Number(BigInt(orderIdStr) >> 64n)` in a try/catch and a `Number.isFinite` check, setting `price = undefined` on any failure. The Order then falls through to marketStats.decodeBidPrice/decodeAskPrice for the failed orderIdStr — i.e. the very fixture-coupled fallback the patch was supposed to retire. So a malformed orderIdStr (or one that exceeds Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER after the right-shift, which is plausible for high-bit ask order_ids — `1n << 127n` shifted right 64 gives `1n << 63n` which is `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER * 1024`, beyond Number range and `Number.isFinite` returns false for it) silently degrades back to the broken bid decode without any log or counter.
impact: On real ask orders (high-bit set), `Number(BigInt(id) >> 64n)` may exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, fail isFinite, set price=undefined, and the marketStats branch then runs decodeAskPrice on the same id — which strips the high bit first, so it returns a different value than the data-layer attempted. The fallback can produce a wrong-but-plausible price that the test suite cannot detect because every fixture has a small ask order_id. There is no log, counter, or assertion to surface the silent fallback.
recommendation: Add a logger.warn or a counter (e.g. `state.book.priceDecodeFailures++`) so the silent fallback is observable. Better: drop the marketStats fallbacks entirely (since iter-3 promised the injection is canonical) and let an undefined price propagate to NaN downstream — that at least surfaces in the rendered card. Best: use BigInt arithmetic throughout marketStats so >2^53 prices stay representable.

title: Iter-3 confirms CR-2 fix is now wired in dataLayer.ts traverseBigVector
description: Confirmation finding for the iter-3 patch. Iter-2 R2-005 (high) flagged that the CR-2 fix declared an Order.price field in marketStats.ts but never populated it from the data layer. Iter-3 added the population in traverseBigVector lines 209-223: every Order constructed from a BigVector slice now has `price` populated via `Number(BigInt(orderIdStr) >> 64n)`. Both production paths (`runDataLayer` and `fetchSinglePoolStats`) flow through traverseBigVector, so every chain-fetched Order now carries a price. computeMarketStats's `o.price !== undefined ? o.price : decodeBidPrice(o.order_id)` branch now selects the injected price for chain inputs. The original iter-2 high (CR-2 cosmetic) is structurally addressed — though see R2-001 (doc/code drift) and R2-011 (silent fallback hazard) for follow-on concerns introduced by the patch.
impact: Iter-2 R2-005 high should be considered closed by this patch. The remaining concerns are about the documentation describing a different design than what shipped, and about the try/catch silently masking decode failures.
recommendation: No action on the wiring itself. Address R2-001 (align comments to actual decode mechanism) and R2-011 (surface decode failures) as separate fixes.
